title: Round 41 New York statewide GNIS source register
scope: New York statewide frame, completing GNIS point coverage of all 50 US states while retaining Buffalo as a separate city frame. 27 exact GNIS rows are screened against the official DomesticNames_NY_Text.zip and retained per-name USGS Geocoder responses. Candidate data are not auto-verified; only exact official name, compatible type, NY state, returned county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and matching primary-point coordinates inside the frame are seeded. The frame and all corridor lines remain schematic context, not state boundary or survey geometry. DomesticNames ZIP SHA-256: 9471de762b1d6bdd7d3f44031b66663568c12a9683b44133e6ee0700f87ab7c8.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. The saved per-name results were screened for exact official Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude; no Geocoder row is VERIFIED by the fetch script.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Official state text extract supplies exact feature names/classes, source-state/county strings, FEATURE_IDs, and GNIS primary points. Each seeded row is matched to the corresponding per-name Geocoder result; water points are not presented as lines or polygons.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 requires exact official name, compatible feature class/Geocoder type, State=NY, matching county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and primary-point latitude/longitude that match across both official USGS surfaces.
DomesticNames county strings are preserved verbatim in the gazetteer row; the Geocoder full county string is preserved separately in the source register.

Only primary points inside the New York frame are seeded. A primary point outside the frame is excluded rather than moved; generalized context lines remain tier=context and are explicitly not feature geometry.
Same-name populated-place, lake, waterfall, and summit records are separate identities and are not collapsed.

The statewide frame uses explicitly synthetic relief and no DEM. Context corridors and the frame bbox are schematic display aids, not state boundaries, surveyed alignments, shorelines, or stream centerlines.

newyork.title: New York statewide frame (Round 41)
newyork.frameNote: Round 41: 27 exact, in-frame GNIS primary points — 16 populated places, five lakes, four streams, and two summits — cross-matched between the New York DomesticNames extract and retained per-name Geocoder responses. The official populated-place spelling is New York; duplicate Lake George, Niagara Falls, and Slide Mountain records are resolved by type/county/point. Several out-of-state or out-of-frame river/lake primary points are excluded rather than moved. Relief and context corridors are schematic, not surveyed geometry.

identityDecisions.candidate: New York City exact-name screen, states=NY
identityDecisions.decision: The USGS Geocoder returned no exact-name candidate and the DomesticNames NY extract has no New York City row. The distinct official Populated Place record is named New York, FEATURE_ID 975772, and is seeded under that verbatim GNIS name.
Seed Lake George as Lake (970163, Lakes & Reservoirs, Warren County); reject the same-name Populated Place record (954913). Both service responses preserve their distinct feature types and points.
Seed Niagara Falls as Populated Place (970406); reject the separate Falls feature (958544). The exact Geocoder type and coordinates distinguish the city from the waterfall.

identityDecisions.candidate: Slide Mountain same-name Summit pile, FEATURE_ID 965414 / 965415 / 975759 / 965413
identityDecisions.decision: Seed only the Ulster County Summit (975759) inside the Catskills frame. Reject the Essex County summits (965414 and 965415) and Warren County summit (965413); all four are exact-name Summit candidates with distinct points.

Do not seed in New York: DomesticNames returns the Lake point in Lake County, Ohio at 42.149115,-81.241010, outside the New York frame. The NY Geocoder query returns Lake Erie Beach populated-place/CDP records, not the lake.
Do not seed: the DomesticNames primary point is in Grand Isle County, Vermont at 44.591152,-73.306344; the NY Geocoder query returns no candidate. No cross-border point is moved into New York.
Do not seed a Lake row: DomesticNames has no Lake Ontario row in the NY candidate extract, and the Geocoder returns only Lake Ontario Ordnance Works (historical), a separate Military feature.

Do not seed: the DomesticNames Stream primary point is in New Castle County, Delaware at 39.432612,-75.528813; the NY Geocoder returns Delaware River Gorge (Valley), not the river. A generalized context corridor is labeled non-GNIS geometry.

Do not seed: the DomesticNames Stream primary point is in Cecil County, Maryland at 39.540391,-76.073839; the NY Geocoder returns Susquehanna River Island, not a Stream. The point is outside the New York frame.

Do not seed despite an exact Geocoder ID/type match: both returned primary points are 49.666667,-64.500556, far outside New York and the frame. Keep only a schematic, explicitly non-GNIS context corridor.

knownLimitations: DomesticNames supplies a single GNIS primary point, not the full geometry of a populated place, lake, river, summit, or state boundary.

The GNIS Geocoder is a fuzzy candidate-discovery surface; the retained records were manually screened by exact ID, name, type, state, county, and coordinates against the official New York DomesticNames text extract.
The statewide terrain is synthetic relief. No DEM, surveyed state outline, water polygon, coastline, shoreline, river centerline, road, or utility alignment is bundled or implied.
New York City was queried as an exact phrase and returned no candidate; the separate official GNIS Populated Place record is named New York and is stored verbatim under that name.

Some border/interstate hydrographic DomesticNames points are outside the New York frame. They remain excluded even when the named feature crosses or borders New York; context corridors are explicitly generalized and non-GNIS.
